name: shell-density-hump
authority: The figure review of the atomic line raised the question (quantum-atom-lab, notes/figure-review-clues-20260922.md, clue 2, and the follow-up recorded as clue 4), and the workspace run out/clue4-shell-hump-criterion.json holds the measurements. This contract authorizes one bounded reconstruction of the criterion and one comparison against those retained measurements, and nothing else.
question: For a shell of an atom of charge Z whose radial density D(r) is built from one effective exponent zeta, when does the shell's density exceed Z itself, and which shells can do so at all?
level: Analytic reconstruction in double precision: the exact hydrogenic radial functions with an explicitly written Laguerre convention, one closed-form criterion zeta/Z > 1/c, a table of c over the K, L and M occupancy patterns, and a comparison against retained finite-basis Hartree-Fock hump positions and values, with six deliberately broken variants and a rejected measurement channel
domain: One shell of an atom of charge Z, its radial density D = 4 pi r^2 rho, the charge-free hydrogenic shape at x = zeta r, the K, L and M occupancy patterns occurring in the workspace, Slater's screening rules applied to the retained shell occupancies, and the twenty-two retained hump rows together with a retained one-row-per-atom scan from H to Ar

objects.shape: shape_{n,occ}(x) = sum_l N_l x^2 Rt_nl(x)^2, where Rt_nl is the charge-free hydrogenic radial shape, so that R_nl(r) = zeta^{3/2} Rt_nl(zeta r) and D(r) = zeta * shape(zeta r)
objects.criterion: D_shell,max > Z if and only if zeta / Z > 1 / c(n, occ), with c = max_x shape and x* = argmax_x shape
objects.k_shell_closed_forms: Rt_10(x) = 2 exp(-x) exactly, hence c = 4/e^2 for one 1s electron and c = 8/e^2 for two, and the hump of either sits at x* = 1 exactly
objects.slater_channel: zeta from Slater's rules applied to the retained per-shell electron counts; the prediction of the sign of (D_max - Z) uses Z, the occupancies and the closed-form table only, and never D_max
objects.position_channel: zeta = x*(pattern) / r*(measured), using only the measured hump position; the hump value forms the answer and never the prediction
objects.value_channel: zeta = D_max / c, retained only to be rejected: it makes the criterion the same statement as D_max > Z

quantifiers: The normalisation integral of every (n, l) shape used, so that the whole c * zeta scaling rests on a checked convention
Every c and x* in the table, recomputed from the analytic shape rather than read from the recorded run
Every retained hump row under both live channels, prediction and measured sign recorded side by side
Every retained row under the value channel, twice, with c perturbed by a relative 1e-3 in the back-solution
Every broken variant, whose failure must be reported rather than asserted
acceptance: The K-shell constants come out as 4/e^2 and 8/e^2 and the K-shell hump at x = 1, so the construction reproduces a case whose answer is known before it is computed
The pure-Python construction reproduces the recorded numpy run of the same formulas to better than 1e-7 in c, and the observed deviation is reported as the number it is
Slater's rules plus the closed-form table predict the measured sign of (D_max - Z) for all twenty-two retained rows, with no fitted parameter and without reading D_max
The hump position alone predicts the same sign for all twenty-two retained rows, so the agreement does not depend on the channel being tautological
The value channel is shown to be information free: a relative perturbation of 1e-3 in c leaves every one of its forty-four verdicts unchanged
The M patterns have c below 1 and the retained M rows stay below Z, so at most the K and L shells exceed Z in this model, and the check fails if either the cap or the measurement moves

(n - 0.30)/Z computed from Slater alone places the first atom with a K-shell hump above Z at Z > 3.9284, and the retained scan places it at Be, whose margin over Z is 1.2e-4 and is reported rather than smoothed
Each of the six broken variants is detected, and the variant that is invisible at the 1s is required to be caught at the 2s
The recorded D_max / Z of every retained row agrees with this file's own D_max divided by Z, and a ratio mistyped by 1e-6 is caught, so the transcription check is not two numbers that always agree
The checker runs under the standard library alone, in one process, with no subprocess
protected: This is not a statement about the true density of any real atom: it is a one-exponent-per-shell hydrogenic model compared against a finite-basis Hartree-Fock density at the measured hump
The retained measurements are not recomputed here. Re-running them needs PySCF, which this checker does not use and cannot use; the rows are evidence carried across, not a second measurement
The argument that at most two shells can exceed Z is an argument inside this model about which shells CAN, and it says nothing about any consequence of the excess
x*(L, 2s2 2p2) landing on 3 + sqrt(3) is an observation at a stated tolerance, not a derivation, and it is not used by any other check
The argmax of a flat maximum is located only to about sqrt(2 * eps) = 2.1e-8 in double precision; that limit is reported, and no check depends on a sharper position
No native certificate, no Rust witness, no Seal, and no admission to any geometry or chemistry catalog follows from this contract
This contract does not authorize a claim about correlation, about the true many-electron density, or about any figure beyond the ones the measurements came from
residual: This gives the observed excess of a shell density over Z a closed-form criterion, a table of constants computed rather than fitted, two independent live channels that agree with the retained measurements on all twenty-two rows, one rejected channel shown to be incapable of disagreement, and a structural reason why only the K and L shells can exceed Z in this model. What it does not do is measure an atom: the measurements are carried across from a workspace run, the model has one exponent per shell where a real atom does not, and the agreement at the atom boundary is thin. The correct next step, if this line continues, is to replace the single exponent by per-l exponents and see whether the twenty-two agreements survive, because that is the assumption the criterion leans on hardest.
